correctness.rationale: At I, one nontrivial cycle gives one neighbor, with binom(n,s)(n-s-1)! neighbors of fixed-set size s. After multiplication by n the normalization is asymptotic to e by the factorial tail, so each fixed-set size tends to Poisson(1). Conditional on both fixed sets and the first cycle, q eligible arrows satisfy n-|A|-2|B| <= q <= n. For each fixed j and bounded fixed-set sizes, j selected arrows cannot close a cycle; contracting the disjoint directed paths yields the falling-factorial moment (q)_j/(n-|B|-1)_j, uniformly tending to 1. All factorial moments determine the Poisson limit; uniformity follows by applying the same moment argument to any sequence of bounded-size conditioning configurations. Tight fixed-set sizes and the st/n bounded-size intersection estimate yield independence of all three limiting Poisson variables, not finite-size independence. The matrix norms and trace give the exact cosine, first-order expansion gives (2M-S-T)/4, and the derivative of arccos gives (S+T-2M)/(2 sqrt(3)). The variances 3/8 and 1/2 are variances of the limiting laws. Sampling with replacement is handled by the proof. The independent check is analytical; the finite package checker was read, not executed, and is not needed for the limit.
residual_risks: No finite-size total-variation rate for the angle or convergence of its scaled moments is certified.
